answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may place jobs or earn reputation. If a bonded agent is caught double-claiming work or colluding in a fraud proof, validators slash its stake, making thousands of disposable identities costly rather than free. A wharf operator might accept only bonded bids; an onyx badge can mark verified stake, while an umber status signals a pending dispute. The defense raises the attacker’s capital cost, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker from buying influence.
